correctness.rationale: Proof of uniform cap five uses the nested marked-star upper bounds for pair families hitting a fixed set of size one, two, three; any triple root negative branch has rank at most four. For n≤9 the positive branch size binom(n−3,2) gives the sharper matching upper bounds. Five explicitly stored complete lower mistake trees for n=5,6,7,8,10 have been traversed independently against actual pair/triple disjointness, certifying 2,4,8,16,32 distinct leaves; monotone embeddings extend lower trees to n=9 and every n≥10. No finite computation is extrapolated to the universal upper bound.

value.rationale: The asymmetric pair/triple disjointness relation is a natural fixed-weight incidence class whose sharp universal online mistake budget of five and first attainment at n=10 are not obtained from symmetric Kneser learning or static VC theory. The marked-star argument and complete lower trees give a useful exact all-n classification, not a cosmetic parameter substitution.
